Prediction: OBBBA Medicaid cuts will push the national health uninsured rate above 9% by end of 2027 as 6-month redeterminations churn eligible beneficiaries off rolls
Invalidation_Criteria: Congress restores Medicaid funding OR courts strike down OBBBA Medicaid provisions
Notes: CBO projects 11.8M losing Medicaid by 2034. First-year impact (2026) likely smaller; 2027 when 6-month churn fully operational. Working-age uninsured already 11.5%.

Prediction: CA FAIR Plan will exceed 750K policies by end of 2026 as 2026 wildfire season reinforces carrier retreat and Sustainable Insurance Strategy proves insufficient to attract major private capacity
Invalidation_Criteria: 6+ major carriers publicly commit to CA with actual volume AND FAIR Plan begins sustained decline
Notes: Growth decelerating (<4% final Q 2025) but CA wildfire season May-Oct 2026 will test. Farmers pledge (300K) is positive but conditional and small. Structural carrier retreat not reversed.

Prediction: FL Citizens will remain below 400K policies through end of 2026 hurricane season, as 2026 forecast (below-normal, El Nino) does not trigger a reversal of the depopulation trend
Invalidation_Criteria: Major hurricane (Cat 3+) makes landfall in FL causing >$25B insured losses
Notes: CSU/AccuWeather: below-normal 2026 season forecast. El Nino developing = wind shear dampening. Risk: it only takes one storm. Confidence is moderate — hurricane forecasting is uncertain.

Prediction: ACA marketplace enrollment will fall below 22M for 2027 plan year absent new subsidy legislation, as premium shock ($178/mo vs $113/mo prior) drives sustained enrollment decline
Invalidation_Criteria: Congress passes and signs ARP-equivalent enhanced premium subsidies before Nov 2026 OE
Notes: First year (2026): 23.1M (-4.9%). Year 2 effect = consumers who stayed in 2026 face another renewal shock. No subsidy legislation currently moving. High confidence in continued decline.

Prediction: Auto insurance combined ratios for Allstate and Progressive will remain below 95% for full-year 2026 as the hard market correction holds and pricing remains adequate
Invalidation_Criteria: Catastrophic storm event causes > $10B auto insurance losses OR litigation costs spike unexpectedly
Notes: 2025: Allstate 85.0, Progressive ~88. Hard market correction well-established. 2026 below-normal hurricane forecast supports. Risk: unexpected SCS (severe convective storm) season or tort surge.

Prediction: Medical debt will contribute to rising consumer bankruptcy filings in 2026, with total bankruptcy filings exceeding 600K (up from 517K in 2024) as ACA cliff removes coverage for 1M+ consumers
Invalidation_Criteria: Medical debt forgiveness at scale OR federal credit reporting protection restored
Notes: 2024: 517K filings (+14.2% from 2023). CFPB rule vacated = no protection. ACA cliff removes 1.2M from coverage. Directionally clear; magnitude uncertain.

Prediction: CA homeowners market will NOT achieve meaningful private sector re-entry in 2026 — FAIR Plan will remain the largest CA residential insurer by policy count, with private carriers' Sustainable Insurance Strategy producing fewer than 50K net new policies from exiting carriers
Invalidation_Criteria: 3+ major carriers announce AND execute re-entry programs exceeding 50K policies combined in CA high-fire areas
Notes: Farmers pledged 5,600 policies over 2 years. CSAA, Mercury seeking rate increases. But exit momentum is structural. $4B loss from single event = actuarially very difficult to price viably. Regulatory risk remains.

Prediction: The combined uninsured + underinsured auto rate will exceed 35% nationally (up from 33.4% in 2023) when next IRC study is published, reflecting the cumulative impact of 5+ years of premium increases outpacing income growth
Invalidation_Criteria: Significant auto premium decrease (>10%) sustained for 2+ years; OR major income gains for bottom 40%
Notes: IRC 2023 data showed 33.4% with trend: "deteriorating insurance affordability more than offsetting economic improvements." Auto premiums +64% cumulative; no reversal of affordability crisis.
